msid_face: Reverse angle of the msid (Quranic school) of the FIRST attached image: same room, same whitewashed walls, painted beam ceiling and straw mats, but now seen from just in front of the master's low wooden platform, looking toward the entrance: a small low wooden door, beside it a wooden shelf full of small children's babouches, writing tablets (planchettes) leaning against the walls, the high small window on the right wall throwing a pale yellow sun patch on the wall, Friday afternoon light. Eye level of a seated child, wide empty mat floor in the foreground.
msid_estrade: Closer view in the same msid (FIRST attached image): the master's low wooden platform covered with a sheepskin against the back wall, a clay inkwell and a small copper pot on it, writing tablets leaning beside it, the small high window up left with afternoon light, straw mats in front. Camera at the eye level of a seated child, a few metres away, empty.
chambre_nuit3: EXACTLY the same room and the same camera angle as the SECOND attached image (same mattresses, cushions, chest, window with the red flowered curtain, niches), at night, BUT the little brass oil lamp on the round table is removed: the only light is one big thick white candle, already burning, in a tall polished copper candlestick standing on the floor beside the low round table. Warm orange candle light near it, deep violet-blue shadows piling up in the corners.
chambre_nuit_porte: Same family room as the SECOND attached image, at night, lit only by one big candle in a tall copper candlestick on the floor near the low round table, but REVERSE ANGLE: seen from the window end, looking toward the tall carved wooden double door standing open onto the dark blue gallery of the patio (wooden balustrade visible outside, a faint white glow from a room across the patio), mattresses with cushions along both side walls, the wooden chest on one side. No oil lamp.
chambre_nuit_lampe: EXACTLY the same room and camera angle as the SECOND attached image, at night, BUT the brass oil lamp on the table is gone and a 1930s kerosene WALL lamp now hangs in the centre of the back wall: brass tin reservoir, tall thin glass chimney shaped like a clarinet, round tin reflector behind it, burning with a calm bright WHITE flame; the room is lit by cool white light, clearer and brighter than candle light, soft shadows.
chambre_jour_lampe: EXACTLY the same room and camera angle as the THIRD attached image (daylight), BUT a brand-new 1930s kerosene wall lamp now hangs in the centre of the back wall above the mattress: brass reservoir, tall clarinet-shaped glass chimney, round shining tin reflector behind it (unlit, daytime).
fatma_nuit: The neighbour's modest room of the FOURTH attached image, but at NIGHT: in the centre of the main wall hangs a 1930s kerosene wall lamp (brass tin reservoir, tall thin glass chimney shaped like a clarinet, round tin reflector mirror behind it) burning with a calm bright WHITE flame that bathes the whole room in white light; reed mat, a few cushions, a clay brazier, simple shelves. Eye level from the doorway, empty floor.
galerie_nuit: Night, eye level ON the second-floor gallery of the patio house of the attached images: wooden balustrade on the left with the dark patio below, a row of doors along the right, deep perspective; at the far end of the gallery one doorway glows with a bright white light spilling onto the floor tiles; blue night elsewhere, a crescent moon above the courtyard.
patio_sol: Midday, the tiled patio of the house of the FIRST attached image seen from GROUND LEVEL, eye level of a standing adult: zellige floor, the well, potted plants, the narrow stone staircase going up on one side, the dark mouth of the entrance corridor, three storeys of wooden galleries above, sun falling into the courtyard.
patio_nattes: The same patio from ground level at noon, prepared for a charity meal: the zellige floor is freshly washed and still wet in places, covered with straw mats and old worn carpets, three large ceramic plates of couscous topped with meat and vegetables on the mats, terracotta water bowls decorated with tar patterns, galleries above, warm sunlight.
couloir_entree: The entrance corridor of the house seen from the patio end: a dim narrow passage with a stone bench, worn zellige floor, at the far end the big studded wooden street door open onto the bright sunlit alley; eye level, empty.
terrasse_feux: The flat rooftop terrace of the SECOND-to-last attached image in bright late morning: outdoor wood fires on stones with big copper cauldrons and an earthenware couscous steamer bubbling and smoking, a big wooden ladle, water jars, a basket of vegetables (carrots, turnips, zucchini) and low stools, laundry line, Fès roofs and a minaret behind.
terrasse_coucher: The same flat rooftop terrace at SUNSET: golden-pink sky, swallows, the sea of Fès roofs and minarets glowing, potted mint and verbena, low parapet; empty open floor.
rahma_chambre: A modest but festive room of a Fès house in the afternoon (same painting style): banquettes with colourful cushions along the walls, low round tables set with dishes (a stew of meat with cardoons, couscous with chickpeas, orange slices with cinnamon), a brass tea tray with a silver teapot and glasses, a door open onto the sunny gallery, a few colourful hangings. Eye level, empty.
ruelle_soir: A narrow medina alley at dusk after rain: dark wet paving stones with reflections, high walls, wooden overhangs, a few lanterns just lit with warm light, deep blue sky strip above, the alley curving away. Eye level of a child, empty.
